newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai opposition leader vows to repair poor economy.
newsitem.headline: Thai opposition leader vows to repair poor economy.

text.p: Former Thai prime minister Chuan Leekpai vowed on Friday to repair the troubled national economy with a strong team of professionals and experts if his party won next month's elections.

The head of the opposition Democrat Party told Reuters that the outgoing administration of premier Banharn Silpa-archa had left the Thai economy in bad shape with sagging exports, a widening current account deficit and high inflation.
The elections will be held on November 17 and the Democrat Party, which now controls 86 of 391 seats in parliament, is said by political analysts to have a good chance of winning the most seats.
It has formed a loose alliance with four other parties, with whom a coalition will be formed if they win the most seats in parliament.
"I will bring more professionals and experts to join the administration," he said.

Key among them were former finance minister and well-known banker Tarrin Nimanhaeminda and former deputy prime minister and central bank official Supachai Panichpakai, who were in his coalition government of 1993-95.

Other political parties, including the New Aspiration Party (NAP) of Defence Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, who is also tipped to be a front-runner for the premiership, have promised a "dream team" to solve the nation's economic woes.
"I don't have a dream team but a real team that will join my administration," said Chuan, apparently cajoling the opposition's use of the "dream team" tag.

He also said many businessmen and the public had become more wary of the need for a government overhaul after troubles hit the national economy during Banharn's administration over the past 14 months.
The stock market has tumbled sharply on uncertainty about what form of government will come into power in the coming polls.

Barnharn dissolved parliament and called new elections last week, angering several factions in his core party which headed a six-party coalition government. He made the surprise move a day before he was due to resign under pressure from several key coalition allies. He is currently caretaker prime minister.
